display.purpose: Page and screen titles, card and modal titles, buttons, badges, table headers. Always uppercase, always tracked.

title.purpose: Entrant names on a match card, activity-feed headings, sub-sections.

body.purpose: Prose, form values, alert bodies, descriptions. The only non-condensed, non-mono role.

label.purpose: Field labels, table metadata, action codes, timestamps, scope/venue lines, trace summaries. Uppercase at 0.75rem.

figure.purpose: Every number that can change while someone is watching: scores, clocks, ranks, stat tiles, numeric columns. Always tabular-nums.

shadows.name: dialog-elevation
shadows.purpose: The only structural shadow in the system. Modals and dialogs, applied once from DIALOG_TOKENS so no screen re-derives its own scrim.

shadows.name: glow-cyan
shadows.purpose: Primary button on hover and active only. Affordance confirming a press, never a state indicator.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Two layers — inner ring in the surface colour, outer in cyan — so the indicator survives dark panels, accent fills, dialogs and image-backed overlays alike. Never clipped to a chamfer.

shadows.name: drawer-scrim
shadows.value: color-mix(in srgb, var(--cl-color-ink-950) 65%, transparent) with backdrop-filter: blur(4px)
shadows.purpose: The mobile navigation drawer's overlay below the md breakpoint.

motion.name: motion-instant
motion.purpose: What every duration collapses to under prefers-reduced-motion. Zero rather than 'shorter': state must survive in text, icon, border and layout, so an animation that merely hurries is one a motion-sensitive viewer still has to endure.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Control state changes — button fill, border colour, file-picker zone.

motion.name: motion-base
motion.purpose: Default transition, and the drawer slide-in duration.

motion.name: motion-flash
motion.purpose: The cyan-well score-change flash. Under reduced motion, animation stops while the cyan well remains for the same 600ms feedback window.

motion.name: motion-pulse
motion.purpose: One opacity phase of each LIVE-dot pulse: the dot fades and returns over successive 2000ms phases, for a 4000ms round trip. Dots start in phase; under reduced motion they stay steady.

motion.name: motion-easing
motion.purpose: Standard easing for every state transition.

motion.name: drawer-easing
motion.purpose: The mobile drawer's slide-in — a sharper decelerating curve than the standard easing.

layout.wideViewport: At widths of 1920px and above, content remains centered at its surface maximum; full-width bands break out while their contents stay aligned to the matching container.

narrative.overview: CopaLibre looks like the gallery behind a live broadcast, not the broadcast itself. The dark theme uses deep ink; L3 Sunlight uses a cool-grey ground and near-white panels while preserving the same semantic roles. Public and Control follow the system preference or an explicit per-device choice, while broadcast remains dark. Across both themes, cyan marks live, primary action, focus, and selection; selected filters use a cyan well with Signal Cyan text and border instead of a primary-action fill. Condensed uppercase labels, tabular monospaced figures, opaque surfaces, and the asymmetric chamfer keep the system precise under tournament pressure.
keyCharacteristics: Flat opaque surfaces: near-black ink in the dark theme and a cool-grey ground with near-white panels in L3
Signal Cyan marks live, primary action, selection, and focus; selected filters use a cyan well rather than the action fill
Public and Control follow the system or an explicit light/dark choice; broadcast remains dark
Condensed uppercase display face for identity; monospace for every figure and label
Asymmetric chamfer (top-right / bottom-left) as the sole shape signature
4px spacing scale, 44px minimum interactive target, tabular figures everywhere numbers appear
Every state carries a text label, icon, border or position alongside its colour
A reserved team-accent slot that organizers may fill and may never use to override a state

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan marks live, primary, selected, or focused state — nothing else outside a chart plot; inside a plot, it means data-series slot 2. A selected filter uses the cyan well with Signal Cyan text and border, not the filled primary-action treatment. A second accent introduced for decoration destroys the only cue an operator scans for across a dense screen.

rules.name: The Never-Colour-Alone Rule
rules.body: Every state token declares a required non-colour companion: state-live carries a LIVE label, state-upcoming a scheduled time, state-positive a result marker, state-destructive an explicit verb or dispute icon. The badge contract throws at build time on a missing label rather than shipping two shades of the same rectangle to a colour-blind viewer.

rules.name: The Protected-State Rule
rules.body: state-live, state-upcoming, state-positive, state-destructive and focus-ring can never be overridden by an organizer's team accent. A team whose colour happens to be red does not get to make "disputed" mean "us".

rules.name: The Opaque-Surface Rule
rules.body: Surface levels are opaque values, never translucent overlays. A composite against an unknown backdrop is a contrast figure nobody can verify.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change while someone is looking at it — a score, a clock, a rank, a stat tile — renders in the mono face with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. A score that shifts width as it changes is a score nobody can read.

rules.name: The Bare Heading Rule
rules.body: Every h1–h6 resolves to the display family without a component asking for it. A heading rendered in the body face is the identity silently not being applied.

rules.name: The Tracked Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text carries tracking from the named scale — wide (0.04em) for metadata and headings, wider (0.05em) for buttons and emphasised labels, widest (0.06em) for the display face set large. Uppercase at normal tracking is a bug, not a choice.

rules.name: The Alternating Band Rule
rules.body: A card over a panel band takes the base fill; the same card over a base band takes the panel fill. Nesting inverts again. A container never sits on its own colour, so structure is readable without a single border being required to carry it.

rules.name: The Chrome-Lifts Rule
rules.body: Chrome — a panel header, a footer, a chip, an icon well — resolves to ink-850 wherever it sits, at any depth. A header reads as a header regardless of what it is nested in.

rules.name: The No-Sideways-Page Rule
rules.body: Wide content scrolls inside its own box (.cl-table-scroll, overflow-x: auto). The page body never scrolls horizontally; every layout child carries min-width: 0.

rules.name: The Shared Container Rule
rules.body: Public, reading and Control content uses the owned centered container at its named maximum, with responsive gutters. At 1920px and wider each surface remains capped and centered. Full-width bands break out while their contents return to the matching container; pages never set a raw max-width.

rules.name: The 44px Rule
rules.body: Every interactive target — button, pill, nav link, form control, pagination step — is at least 44px in its constrained axis.

rules.name: The Flat-Unless-Suspended Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. Shadow appears only where an element is suspended above the page (a dialog) or is confirming a press (the primary button). A resting card with a shadow is drift.

rules.name: The Two-Layer Focus Rule
rules.body: The focus indicator is always two rings, never one, and never clipped to a chamfer — clip-path is prohibited for corner geometry precisely so that outside-the-box indicators survive.

rules.name: The No-Mask Rule
rules.body: Chamfer geometry is corner-shape and border-radius only. A polygon mask clips the focus ring and the glow, which is exactly what the accessibility gate cannot allow.

rules.name: The Diagonal-Pair Rule
rules.body: The default cut is top-right and bottom-left. Any other combination is a declared variant, not an ad hoc choice at the call site.

rules.name: The Equal Sides Rule
rules.body: The featured TV match gives home and away identical square emblem frames and the same content order: emblem, entrant name, localized role tag. The neutral tag names each side; size, placement and accent colour never imply preference.

rules.name: The First-Viewport Rule
rules.body: Give each screen one focal point in its first viewport. Public tournament overviews lead with live matches, then the next fixtures and latest results; Control dashboards lead with tournaments that need action.

rules.name: The Match-Summary Rule
rules.body: Show up to four upcoming fixtures and four latest results on a tournament overview, then link to the complete match list. Use full entrant names in the overview and abbreviations in tickers.

rules.name: The Neutral-Progress Rule
rules.body: Use LIVE and its live colour only for a match in play. An underway tournament uses a neutral In progress badge. Upcoming matches have no score; show a dash and pair an empty live state with the next kickoff time.

rules.name: The Progressive-Disclosure Rule
rules.body: Schedules group matches by day and venue, with collapsible days and filters. Standings reveal tie-break detail for one position at a time. Activity feeds group consecutive identical actions while preserving the complete audit trail.

rules.name: The Action-Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Give each view region one primary action; supporting actions use secondary or tertiary treatment. Keep figures at the figure token with a minimum size of 1.875rem and labels at 0.75rem.

rules.name: The Linked-Card Rule
rules.body: For linked cards, make the title the link and use one overlay hit target for the remaining card area. Keep non-link text visually unadorned.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Cyan Rule
rules.body: Do not use cyan for decoration, including taglines, rails, or resting glows.

rules.name: The Chart-and-Table Rule
rules.body: Charts identify each series by entity name and provide the same values in a table. Forms show validation only after a field is blurred or submitted, never on first render.

dos: Do name a state, never a colour. Components consume state-live, not cyan-400, so retheming "live" is one line in semantic.ts rather than a search across three rendering technologies.
Do pair every state colour with its declared non-colour cue — a LIVE label, a scheduled time, a result marker, an explicit verb.
Do render every changeable number in the mono face with tabular-nums.
Do cut the chamfer with corner-shape and border-radius, and let unsupported browsers get square corners and a working component.
Do keep interactive targets at 44px in the constrained axis, and let long labels wrap with overflow-wrap: anywhere rather than overflow — interface copy must survive all eight languages.
Do let containers alternate against their band, and let chrome lift to ink-850 at any depth.
Do compose the shared layout container for page width and gutters; let full-width bands break out around aligned contents.
Do collapse motion to 0s under prefers-reduced-motion, not merely shorten it: state must survive in text, icon, border and layout without the animation.
Do keep the TV spotlight symmetrical: equal emblem frames and a localized neutral role tag beneath each name.
Do scroll wide content inside its own box.
Do give each screen one first-viewport focal point and keep tournament summaries to four upcoming fixtures and four latest results before linking to complete lists.
Do use the cyan well with Signal Cyan text and border for selected filters, reserving filled cyan for primary actions.
Do order fixtures chronologically within rounds and cups by promotion tier; use full entrant names on overviews and abbreviations in tickers.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent colour. Cyan is the only voice, and its scarcity is what makes it scannable. Data-visualization plot areas are the named exception: they may use only the five declared series colours; chart chrome remains in ink and text tokens.
Don't use clip-path for corner geometry. It clips the focus ring and the glow.
Don't use emblem size, accent colour or placement to imply that either side of the TV match is more important.
Don't let an organizer's team accent reach state-live, state-upcoming, state-positive, state-destructive or focus-ring, or appear in core chrome — navigation, primary buttons, system badges.
Don't ship a badge, chip or status mark whose only signal is its colour.
Don't add a resting shadow. Shadow means suspended (a dialog) or pressed (the primary button).
Don't use translucent surface fills where a row's contrast has to be verifiable; resolve them to opaque tokens.
Don't set page-level max-width or horizontal gutter values by hand; use the named layout containers and tokens.
Don't reach for text-muted for body copy — it is a label colour.

Don't reintroduce SebaSOFT's identity: #f3e600, #c5003c, CP2077 or DATA_BLOB vocabulary, TRON references, scanlines, or a grid glow used as a state indicator. CI scans generated output for all of them.
Don't introduce a spacing, radius, font-size, tracking or breakpoint value outside the named scales. A hardcoded literal at a call site is how a scale becomes an accident.
Do not expose filter, tab, or sort controls inside a read-only overview standings summary.
Do not use LIVE for an underway tournament when no match is in play; use the neutral In progress state.
Do not use cyan for decorative taglines, rails, or resting glows.
